transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-15 14:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (CSM), Jordan (Harbor Tech Head ML), Sasha (Platform Eng), Evan (FinOps)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): QBR focused on SLA and cost efficiency; plan benchmark and pilot; clarifications on quantization impact to accuracy.

00:00 Alex Ramos: Okay thanks everyone for joining, um we're gonna kick off the QBR — quick round of intros, then we'll go into the latency/error budget review.
00:18 Jordan Lee: Hey Alex, Jordan here — we're excited, been seeing a couple spikes in latency during the mornings.
00:25 Sasha Patel: Sasha — platform, we've also got a couple infra requests around private VPC routing for PII flows.
00:33 Alex Ramos: Great, thanks. Priya, do you want to run the SLA slide real quick?
00:38 Priya Singh: Sure, yeah so current SLA target you guys set is 95th percentile under 220 ms for the reply latency on the suggestions endpoint — looking at the last quarter the measured p95 is ~310 ms during peak windows, so we've got about a 90 ms gap. Some of that is queuing, some is cold start on smaller clusters.
01:05 Sasha Patel: We're seeing bursty traffic from 07:00 to 09:30 PT, about 3x baseline, and our autoscale doesn't fully catch up because of the conservative scale-up policy. Also the KV cache seems to drop more often than we'd like — I think it's the K V cash TTL setting?
01:28 Priya Singh: Yeah the K-V cache TTL is 45s currently, maybe too short for your workload. We can recommend prefix caching for the conversational flows, and also bump the warm pool for the dedicated fleet.
01:43 Evan Murphy: From a finance perspective, any warm pool increase is gonna add committed cost, we need clear unit economics before we sign up for bigger pools.
01:52 Alex Ramos: Totally understood. This is where the cost/perf tuning comes in — we have a couple levers: batching, quantization, codegen model vs instruction-tuned, and dedicated warm pools. We'll run a benchmark to show tradeoffs.
02:05 Jordan Lee: Quick question on quantization — last time we tried 4-bit it introduced hallucination increases on the rerank model. Is that expected?
02:15 Priya Singh: Good q. In our experience 4-bit (PTQ) on that particular architecture increases token-level noise for long-context reranking; we usually recommend mixed approach: int8 for generator, and keep reranker at fp16 or q4f16 if available. We'll attach a more detailed mapping.
02:36 Sasha Patel: Also need the audit logs for private deployment — we have SOC2 audit coming in Q4. How detailed are the request/response logs? We need redaction hooks.
02:47 Daniel Cho: We can provide per-request metadata and config traces; full response logging is optional and we support field-level redaction and KMS-managed encryption. We'll surface the security pack after the call.
03:02 Alex Ramos: Let's talk benchmarks — Priya, plan?
03:06 Priya Singh: Plan is a 48-hour run: mirror a small percentage of production traffic (1-2%), run variants: hosted baseline (current config), hosted + batching 32/64, hosted + int8 quant, dedicated warm pool 2x. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy deltas on sample eval set. We'll provide scripts and a results spreadsheet.
03:33 Jordan Lee: Will you also capture tail latency cause — like GPU queue depth? That's our main pain.
03:39 Priya Singh: Yes, we'll instrument queue depth and kernel wait times; though the trace names may differ slightly, the trace will show CPU -> GPU handoff.
03:50 Sasha Patel: For private deployment, network egress is a question — can we avoid egress to Redwood's hosted control plane? We need control plane mirrors or on-prem control plane.
04:01 Alex Ramos: Short answer: we offer Private with customer-managed control plane options, or VPC endpoints to minimize egress. For fully air-gapped we have an on-prem package but that takes longer to stand up.
04:15 Evan Murphy: Timelines? For our SOC2 we need Private or VPC by mid-Oct. Is that realistic?
04:21 Priya Singh: VPC endpoints + KMS integration is realistic by mid-Oct for a standard pilot assuming approvals; on-prem full air-gap likely a multi-quarter project.
04:33 Jordan Lee: Cool. On the cost side, Evan wants to model three scenarios: conservative (hosted with batching), aggressive (dedicated + warm pools), and hybrid (private endpoints with int8).
04:45 Evan Murphy: Yep. Also curious about credits for pilot or discounts on committed capacity for first 3 months.
04:52 Alex Ramos: We can propose a pilot credit and a short-term committed discount for the initial quarter — I'll attach options.
04:58 Sasha Patel: One more engineering ask — our infra team needs a runbook for rolling fallback: when the primary model degrades, route to a smaller faster model gracefully. Do you support routing policies at request-level?
05:11 Priya Singh: Yes, smart routing can fallback by latency, region, or model variant; we can set up canary policies and automatic fallback to a lower-tier model with an explainability tag in the trace.
05:26 Jordan Lee: Anything else on performance?
05:29 Priya Singh: We'll also test KV cache warmers and prefix caching. For some of your templates, prefix reuse hit rate is low — optimizing prompt templates reduces token cost by about 8-12% in similar customers.
05:49 Evan Murphy: Good to know. Would you include an estimated cost delta per month in the benchmark?
05:55 Priya Singh: Yes, cost per 1k tokens and projected monthly burn based on your token histogram.
06:03 Alex Ramos: Let's capture open risks: SOC2 timeline, Hallucination/accuracy with lower-precision models, and peak autoscale behavior.
06:12 Jordan Lee: I also worry about A/B regressions when we switch model variants; need evals tied to our prompt set.
06:20 Priya Singh: We'll run regression tests against your eval prompts and give confidence intervals. If we see >1.5% accuracy delta we'll recommend against the change. That's configurable.
06:33 Sasha Patel: For the pilot scope — what's the minimal footprint? We can start with 3 routes: suggestions, rerank, and short-form content. Keep PII routed to private endpoints.
06:45 Alex Ramos: Sounds good. Priya will own the benchmark; Jordan will share prompt mix; Alex will send invite and security artifacts.
06:52 Daniel Cho: I'll follow up with the security pack and the SAML/SSO integration steps.
06:58 Alex Ramos: Alright let's do quick recap and next steps...
07:04 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone.
07:06 Alex Ramos: Thanks — we'll send the benchmark runbook and invite.
07:10 (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: speaker turns roughly aligned but some technical terms may be mistranscribed (e.g., "K-V cache" -> "K V cash", "int8" spelled as "in t eight" in raw audio). There are a few overlaps and filler words preserved.
